extracted.intended_audience: patent bar examinees, patent practitioners, and applicants preparing or prosecuting U.S. design patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and statutory/regulatory standards for preparing, filing, and examining U.S. design patent applications (what makes a design patentable, required application elements, and prosecution topics). Intended to guide applicants and examiners in meeting U.S. design patent requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent subject matter (general definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patents protect the ornamental appearance or aesthetic design of a functional item, rather than its utility or functional aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The design must be embodied in or applied to an article or manufacture; it cannot exist alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Design (1502)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1502: Definition of a Design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers the statutory and doctrinal meaning of what constitutes a 'design' for purposes of design patents (ornamentality, association with an article of manufacture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between design and utility patents (1502.01 / key term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patents protect how an article "looks" as opposed to how an article "works" (which is provided in a utility patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this distinction when determining whether protection should be sought via a design or utility application; see related guidance under 'Utility Patent'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that design be embodied in an article
rubrics_metrics.description: The design must be embodied in or applied to an article or manufacture; it cannot exist alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claimed design must be for an article of manufacture — abstract designs not applied to articles are not proper design patent subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting (key term / 1504.06)
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting refers to the prohibition against an inventor holding two patents for the same invention or for obvious variations of the same invention, to prevent unjustified extension of patent rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses how double-patenting principles apply in the design patent context and the prohibition's effect on prosecution and claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination (key term / 1504.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expedited examination is a process that accelerates the review of a patent application, allowing it to be examined more quickly than under standard procedures, often in exchange for an additional fee or meeting specific criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1504.30 addresses procedures and criteria for obtaining expedited examination of a design application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (key term / 1504.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty refers to the requirement that an invention must be new and not previously known or used by others before the date of the patent application to qualify for patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1504.02 covers application of novelty (35 U.S.C. § 102) to design patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification (1503.01 / key term)
rubrics_metrics.description: A specification is a detailed written description of an invention in a patent application, explaining how it works and how to make and use it, which is essential for defining the scope of the patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1503.01 addresses the specification element of a design application — what descriptive material is required or permitted in a design application (titles, descriptions, feature-identifying text, disclaimers, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings or photographs requirement (37 CFR 1.152 / 1503.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.152 specifies that design patent applications must include drawings or photographs that clearly depict the design's appearance, showing all features of the claimed design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1503.02 (Drawings) explains acceptable drawing conventions, viewpoints, shading, broken lines, and photographic submissions for clearly showing the claimed ornamental features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of application elements (37 CFR 1.154)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.154 outlines the required order and arrangement of elements in a design patent application, including the title, description, drawings or photographs, and any necessary disclaimers or other statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1.154 guidance dictates the proper sequence and formatting of application parts to comply with USPTO filing rules for design applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory basis for design patents (35 U.S.C. 171)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 171 establishes that patents can be granted for new, original, and ornamental designs for an article of manufacture, subject to the conditions and requirements of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the statutory authority and basic statutory standards (new, original, ornamental) for grant of design patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of design patent (35 U.S.C. 173 / section 1505)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 173 specifies that the term of a design patent is 15 years from the date of grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1505 restates and explains term calculation and related procedural points for design patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of a design patent application (1503)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1503: Elements of a Design Patent Application Filed Under 35 U.S.C. chapter 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists required elements such as specification (1503.01) and drawings (1503.02), and explains what must be included in each element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory subject matter issues for designs (1504.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1504.01: Statutory Subject Matter for Designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers what designs qualify as statutory subject matter and addresses borderline or special categories (see subparts a–e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer-generated icons (1504.01(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: 1504.01(a) — Considerations specific to computer-generated icons as design patent subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses when and how GUI/icon designs are eligible for design patent protection and issues unique to depicting screen-based designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design comprising multiple articles or multiple parts embodied in a single article (1504.01(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 1504.01(b) — Treatment of designs that claim multiple articles or multiple parts embodied in a single article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses how to claim and depict multi-part designs, whether divided claims or multiple figures are required, and how ornamentality is considered across parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of ornamentality (1504.01(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: 1504.01(c) — Lack of ornamentality as a ground for refusal (i.e., designs that are primarily functional rather than ornamental).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how examiners determine whether a feature is ornamental vs functional and when a design lacks ornamentality sufficient for patent protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulation (1504.01(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: 1504.01(d) — Issues relating to simulation (representations that simulate the appearance rather than the actual article).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on acceptability of simulated views (e.g., perspective vs. actual appearance) and limitations on representations that are not faithful to the claimed article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offensive subject matter (1504.01(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: 1504.01(e) — Treatment of designs that may be considered offensive subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how offensive or immoral subject matter is handled in the design patent context (grounds for refusal or special handling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty analysis for designs (1504.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1504.02 addresses novelty (newness) requirements applicable to design patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to compare prior art designs, effect of prior public disclosures, and what constitutes anticipation of an ornamental design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonobviousness for designs (1504.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1504.03 covers nonobviousness (35 U.S.C. § 103) as applied to ornamental designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses the standard for assessing whether a design is an obvious variation of the prior art and relevant factors in the design context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations under 35 U.S.C. 112 for design applications (1504.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1504.04: Considerations under 35 U.S.C. 112 (written description, definiteness, etc.) as applied to design patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses how written description/definiteness requirements are satisfied for design claims, the role of drawings vs. text, and permissible claim scope language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice for designs (1504.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1504.05 covers restriction — when an examiner may require restriction into distinct inventions in a design application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains criteria for making restriction requirements, candidate situations (e.g., multiple distinct designs claimed), and how applicants can respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claims (35 U.S.C. 119 / 1504.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1504.10: Priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d), 386(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains requirements and effects of claiming foreign priority or benefit to earlier-filed applications for design patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 (1504.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1504.20: Benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on claiming benefit to earlier U.S. provisional/nonprovisional applications and the requirements in the design context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term and related issues (1505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1505: Term of Design Patent (practical and statutory aspects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains statutory term (see 35 U.S.C. 173) and practical considerations affecting enforceable term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue of a design patent (1509)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1509: Reissue of a Design Patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains circumstances and procedure for reissuing a design patent (corrections of errors and scope adjustments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination (1510)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1510: Reexamination procedures as applied to design patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers grounds, timing, and effects of reexamination requests for issued design patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest procedures (1511)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1511: Protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains procedures by which third parties may submit protests or information during design patent prosecution and the handling thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between design patent, copyright, and trademark (1512)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1512: Relationship Between Design Patent, Copyright, and Trademark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses overlap, differences, and interactions among design patent protection, copyright protection, and trademark law for ornamental designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous topics (1513)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1513: Miscellaneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers additional, varied topics relevant to design patent practice not captured in the other sections.
